blocks: ## How to use this reference
A reference for comparing patterns, not a list to memorise in one sitting.

Use this page after studying individual forms. It brings together regular sound-root models, common verbal-noun patterns and participles. The tables are a guide to recognition and analysis; actual verb meanings and irregular forms must still be learned from reliable vocabulary entries.

[callout] Scope: These are the ten commonly taught numbered families of triliteral verbs. Arabic also has quadriliteral verbs, weak-root changes and other patterns. A root need not occur in every family, and a theoretically possible form is not necessarily a word in normal use.
## The ten patterns
Read each past/present pair alongside a real example.

TABLE: Form | Past pattern | Present pattern | Example pair // I | فَعَلَ | يَفْعُلُ | كَتَبَ / يَكْتُبُ // II | فَعَّلَ | يُفَعِّلُ | عَلَّمَ / يُعَلِّمُ // III | فَاعَلَ | يُفَاعِلُ | شَارَكَ / يُشَارِكُ // IV | أَفْعَلَ | يُفْعِلُ | أَرْسَلَ / يُرْسِلُ // V | تَفَعَّلَ | يَتَفَعَّلُ | تَعَلَّمَ / يَتَعَلَّمُ // VI | تَفَاعَلَ | يَتَفَاعَلُ | تَعَاوَنَ / يَتَعَاوَنُ // VII | اِنْفَعَلَ | يَنْفَعِلُ | اِنْكَسَرَ / يَنْكَسِرُ // VIII | اِفْتَعَلَ | يَفْتَعِلُ | اِكْتَسَبَ / يَكْتَسِبُ // IX | اِفْعَلَّ | يَفْعَلُّ | اِحْمَرَّ / يَحْمَرُّ // X | اِسْتَفْعَلَ | يَسْتَفْعِلُ | اِسْتَعْمَلَ / يَسْتَعْمِلُ

[callout] Form I: The displayed يَفْعُلُ is one common present pattern. Other families include يَفْعِلُ and يَفْعَلُ. Learn each verb’s past–present pair; do not infer it from the past spelling alone.
## Verbal nouns and participles
See how a verb can be related to an action noun, a doer or an affected thing.

A verbal noun (maṣdar) names an action or process. An active participle can identify a doer or describe a state. A passive participle can describe something affected by an action. These are morphological categories, not guaranteed English translations.

TABLE: Form | Common verbal noun pattern | Active participle pattern | Passive participle pattern // I | Varies; learn individually | فَاعِلٌ | مَفْعُولٌ // II | تَفْعِيلٌ | مُفَعِّلٌ | مُفَعَّلٌ // III | مُفَاعَلَةٌ / فِعَالٌ | مُفَاعِلٌ | مُفَاعَلٌ // IV | إِفْعَالٌ | مُفْعِلٌ | مُفْعَلٌ // V | تَفَعُّلٌ | مُتَفَعِّلٌ | مُتَفَعَّلٌ // VI | تَفَاعُلٌ | مُتَفَاعِلٌ | Not normally used with intransitive models // VII | اِنْفِعَالٌ | مُنْفَعِلٌ | Not normally used with intransitive models // VIII | اِفْتِعَالٌ | مُفْتَعِلٌ | مُفْتَعَلٌ // IX | اِفْعِلَالٌ | مُفْعَلٌّ | Not normally used // X | اِسْتِفْعَالٌ | مُسْتَفْعِلٌ | مُسْتَفْعَلٌ

[callout] Use, not just shape: Passive participles are not equally natural or common for every verb. Intransitive verbs often have no ordinary passive participle. Some apparent active/passive forms coincide after weak-root changes. Always check the actual lexical entry before using a derived noun.

TABLE: Verb | Verbal noun | Active participle | Passive participle // كَتَبَ | كِتَابَةٌ | كَاتِبٌ | مَكْتُوبٌ // عَلَّمَ | تَعْلِيمٌ | مُعَلِّمٌ | مُعَلَّمٌ // شَارَكَ | مُشَارَكَةٌ | مُشَارِكٌ | — // أَرْسَلَ | إِرْسَالٌ | مُرْسِلٌ | مُرْسَلٌ // تَعَلَّمَ | تَعَلُّمٌ | مُتَعَلِّمٌ | — // تَعَاوَنَ | تَعَاوُنٌ | مُتَعَاوِنٌ | — // اِنْكَسَرَ | اِنْكِسَارٌ | مُنْكَسِرٌ | — // اِكْتَسَبَ | اِكْتِسَابٌ | مُكْتَسِبٌ | مُكْتَسَبٌ // اِحْمَرَّ | اِحْمِرَارٌ | مُحْمَرٌّ | — // اِسْتَعْمَلَ | اِسْتِعْمَالٌ | مُسْتَعْمِلٌ | مُسْتَعْمَلٌ
A dash means that an ordinary passive participle is not supplied for this model; it does not assert that no related form can exist in any context.
## Important exceptions and distinctions
Regular patterns are a starting point, not a substitute for lexical knowledge.
### Form I vowels
Learn كَتَبَ / يَكْتُبُ، فَهِمَ / يَفْهَمُ، جَلَسَ / يَجْلِسُ as complete pairs. Form I maṣdars are often lexical.
### Weak and hamzated roots
Hollow, final-weak and hamzated verbs may contract or change spelling. Compare قَالَ / يَقُولُ، اِخْتَارَ / يَخْتَارُ .
### Form VIII assimilation
The inserted ت can assimilate or change near certain root consonants. The root and lexical pair explain surface forms such as اِتَّصَلَ / يَتَّصِلُ .
### Form VII and passive
اِنْكَسَرَ الْكَأْسُ. is Form VII. كُسِرَ الْكَأْسُ. is the grammatical passive of Form I. They are not the same construction.

[callout] Imperatives: The imperative is derived from the appropriate present stem, with root-specific changes. Examples include اُكْتُبْ، عَلِّمْ، شَارِكْ، أَرْسِلْ، تَعَلَّمْ، تَعَاوَنْ، اِنْصَرِفْ، اِكْتَسِبْ، اِسْتَعْمِلْ . Form IX imperatives are not part of the ordinary core reference.
For full tense, person, passive-voice and participle teaching, return to the existing Verbs collection . This reference does not replace those lessons.
## Reference self-check
Use the tables to repair any uncertainties, then retry.
## Your next step
### Use the reference selectively
- recognise the characteristic past and present patterns;
- distinguish verbal nouns, active participles and passive participles;
- allow for weak roots, assimilation and lexical exceptions;
- return to an individual form whenever a pattern needs more practice.
